notes: A convention catalog defines mathDef's adopted meaning and notes; source assessments elsewhere describe external authors.
Canonical meaning is resolved against the *current* catalog via canonical_meaning_id, not embedded as a frozen operational predicate.

entries.canonical_policy: No separation into two disjoint nonempty open subsets covering X, including X=empty.
entries.rationale: The no-separation predicate is meaningful and vacuously true on the empty space. mathDef includes it; some sources explicitly require nonemptiness.
entries.note: Some authors require connected spaces to be nonempty. mathDef uses the no-separation condition, which includes the empty space.

entries.canonical_policy: The induced topology on A is {A∩U:U open in X} for every A⊆X, including A=∅.
entries.rationale: The induced-topology construction works for ∅, but some authors restrict the word subspace by their nonempty-space convention; this is not a new topology construction.
entries.note: The subspace topology is defined on the empty subset as well. Sources assuming nonempty topological spaces may exclude it by convention.

entries.boundary_object: element 0 in a nonzero commutative ring
entries.canonical_policy: Zero divisors must be nonzero: a≠0 and there is b≠0 with ab=0.
entries.rationale: User mathematical adjudication 2026-10-27. Some conventions call zero a zero divisor in a nonzero ring; mathDef explicitly excludes it. This is an editorial choice, not a blanket statement about all sources.
entries.note: mathDef requires zero divisors to be nonzero; 0 is not a zero divisor. Other sources sometimes allow zero as a zero divisor.

entries.canonical_policy: A metric space (X,d) requires X≠∅ in addition to the metric axioms.
entries.rationale: User adjudication 2026-10-27. The unique metric on the empty set satisfies the axioms vacuously but is not called a metric space in mathDef; no global attribution to a source's convention is inferred.
entries.note: mathDef requires the underlying set of a metric space to be nonempty; some authors also allow the empty space.

entries.boundary_object: empty subset S of an affine space
entries.canonical_policy: Affine span and affine hull name the same nonempty-input construction; S must be nonempty, and aff(∅) is not defined by mathDef.
entries.rationale: User adjudication 2026-10-27. Use both terms as searchable synonyms, traditionally with differing algebra/analysis emphasis; preserve both combination and intersection characterizations. Do not claim excluded empty hull is mathematically impossible.
entries.note: mathDef defines the affine span/hull of nonempty sets only. Alternative conventions set the hull of the empty set to the empty set.
